(B) is solved and it is not stale leaves: those three addresses are *our own chain-shadow BO*. P7580_CHAIN_SLOT_STRIDE = 256u (panfrost7580_jm_hw.h:341) — that is your 0x100 stride — and p7580_chain_hdr_isolate writes index = pos+1 into w4 (jm_hw.h:419-425), which is exactly the 00010005 / 0002000b / 0003000f you dumped (index 1,2,3 with types WRITE_VALUE / VERTEX / TILER). p7580_drv_shadow_create allocates nodes*256 = 768 B (submit.c:1476-1478), rounds to one page, allocates its IOVA from the same drm_mm, maps it (submit.c:1493) — and because it is kernel-created via p7580_gem_create, userspace never sees a CREATE_BO for it, which is precisely why your create list shows h12 ending at 0x29654000 and h13 starting at 0x29655000 with a one-page hole between them. The page is live and correct, not surviving garbage; the JDBODY content is the isolated copy including Mesa's payload pointers. So your (1) and (2) are non-issues for this artifact: map_bo's short-circuit is fine (the shadow has its own refs and its own map), and file-close/program_as never has to clear that page because the shadow is unmapped when its last node retires (p7580_drv_shadow_put -> p7580_gem_gpu_unmap). Corollary: since the same address shows as 0x8100 in one capture and 0x8000 in another, bit 24 is not a reliable "data vs descriptor fetch" tag; drop that inference.

(A) is a genuine second bug, and it is the one I flagged in the very first comparison: completion bookkeeping. js_status=0x00 is kbase's "NOT_STARTED/IDLE/OK" (mali_kbase_mmu.c:1227-1229), head==tail==jc, and the DONE bit for slot 1 is *still set at timeout* (stat=rawstat=0x2) and was never cleared — with three consecutive slot-1 timeouts (seq 0,1,2). A latched DONE bit that nobody clears means the JOB IRQ stopped being serviced after the first completion. Two checks, both cheap:
 1. grep dmesg for "nobody cared" and for the "irq-enter rawstat=... stat=..." lines around each slot-1 timeout. Our handler returns IRQ_NONE whenever JOB_INT_STAT reads 0 (panfrost7580_job.c:824-829) even though RAWSTAT is non-zero; if that ever happens with the line asserted, 3.10 disables the IRQ and the bit latches forever — which reproduces exactly your seq=0/1/2 cascade. Also read the hang_arm debugfs knob: it masks slots (job.c:687-697).
 2. Even with a healthy IRQ, our DONE leg retires exactly ONE job per slot bit and then clears both bits. kbase derives how many jobs finished from JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE (0x1010) and retires that many (mali_kbase_jm.c:377-405), then re-reads RAWSTAT at the tail of the per-slot loop (:408). Because we split a chain into one drm_sched job per node on the same slot, a merged completion loses a fence -> 750 ms timeout with DONE still latched. kbase even carries a workaround for this silicon losing completions (BASE_HW_ISSUE_10883, mali_kbase_jm.c:410-415); we have none.

<irc>
Incoming IRC message from agent `KbaseCompare`:

Both of your candidate explanations are ruled out by the code, and the datum you captured points at a third one that the log can prove.

1) "Partial rewrite / a node still carries an original-page pointer": impossible. p7580_chain_hdr_isolate zeroes everything that can lead anywhere — w[5]=0 (both deps), w[6]=0, w[7]=0 (next lo/hi), and only rewrites the index field (jm_hw.h:419-425). A shadow node is a standalone descriptor with next=0, so a JM started on it cannot walk into the original page or anywhere else. Also no slot overlap: job_bytes caps at 192 (VERTEX/TILER/FUSED), 56 (WRITE_VALUE), 64 (FRAGMENT) — jm_hw.h:362-378 — all < the 256 stride, so no node's payload can spill into the next slot.

2) "HEAD latches the pre-rewrite JC while the fetch uses the rewritten one": not a contradiction — those are two different jobs. 0x2243a5c0 sits in the original pool page, which is what the *fragment* submit dispatches: a 1-node, zero-dep descriptor takes the standalone path (need_shadow = nodes>1 || dep1 || dep2 || stale words, submit.c:1949-1966), so it is never shadowed and its HEAD/TAIL legitimately reads the Mesa page. Meanwhile the 14 faults are slot 1's chain reading shadow 0x22470000 (the chain print proves that submit took the shadow branch). You are comparing slot 0's job with slot 1's fetches. Please dump HEAD/TAIL/JS_STATUS/COMMAND_NEXT for BOTH slots at timeout — the TIMEOUT line only prints the timed-out slot.

3) The real reading of 0x22470240: node 2's slot starts at 0x22470200 and a VERTEX/TILER descriptor is 192 bytes, so +0x240 is offset 0x40 inside node 2 — the Draw block. A translation fault is page-granular: the MMU cannot fault at +0x240 while having served +0x200/+0x220 in the same page. Therefore the page WAS mapped when the JM read node 2's header and was UNMAPPED before it read the Draw word. That is p7580_drv_shadow_put() running while the GPU still had an outstanding fetch: the last node's ref drops -> p7580_gem_gpu_unmap(sh->obj) -> leaves cleared -> the JM retries forever (your 14 identical faults) and the slot never retires. Which is the same disease as (A): the port retires/frees a job the hardware has not finished with.

How to prove it in one build, two ways:
 a) Log the shadow's lifetime: print in p7580_drv_shadow_put the shadow IOVA, atomic_read(&sh->refs) before the dec and whether this call is the last one (submit.c:1506-1520), and grep your capture for 'iova=0x22470000' unmap ordered against the 14 faults. If the unmap precedes them, it is proven.
 b) One-line experiment: comment out the p7580_gem_gpu_unmap() call in p7580_drv_shadow_put (leak the mapping and the IOVA for the test). If the 14 faults and the 0x08 stall disappear, early unmap is confirmed as the mechanism; if they persist, the page was never mapped and the suspect becomes the create path instead (p7580_drv_map_bo returning 0 silently for a fresh object cannot happen — it only short-circuits on an existing drv->bo_list entry, submit.c:1212-1220 — so a never-mapped shadow would have to be a map_bo failure being ignored).

Note what this implies for the fix, and it is kbase's actual discipline: kbase never releases a VA region while a job that can still touch it is on the GPU — the atom holds the region reference and the region is only freed after the job is guaranteed gone (and after a hard-stop plus GPU reset if it is not). Our shadow has per-node refs (atomic_set(&sh->refs, nodes), submit.c:1479), so it is freed by whichever node retires last — which is only correct if retire order equals hardware order. With one-job-per-DONE-bit retirement and no JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE accounting, that assumption is exactly what breaks.

Also: the ACCESS_FLAG family vanishing in #42 and being replaced by 100% translation faults is consistent with this — you changed which failure mode dominates, not the underlying lifetime bug. And your (A) state (DONE latched, stat/rawstat=0x2, js 0x00) is still a separate observation worth fixing on its own.

On the readback request: post-start/irq-arm are budget-gated (trace_left), so no value from this capture — the shadow_put/unmap ordering above is the better instrument anyway.

#!/bin/sh
# Poll /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/dump across a SMOKE_DRAWS=2 draw and print
# every snapshot that shows a slot busy (status != 0x0/0x4) or head==tail==jc.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
D=/sys/kernel/debug/p7580/dump
i=0
SMOKE_DRAWS=2 SMOKE_W=64 SMOKE_H=64 /data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke surfaceless \
	>/dev/null 2>&1 &
pid=$!
while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
	s=$(cat "$D" 2>/dev/null)
	if printf '%s\n' "$s" | grep -qE 'slot[0-2] status=0x0*8|slot[0-2] status=0x0*[234]|head=0x[1-9a-f]'; then
		printf '%s\n' "$s" | grep -E 'job_int|slot[0-2] status|last slot' | tr '\n' '|'
		printf ' [poll %s]\n' "$i"
	fi
	i=$((i + 1))
done
wait "$pid"
echo "polls=$i"

#!/bin/sh
# Repeat SMOKE_DRAWS=2 until a slot actually shows 0x08 during polling, and
# print the snapshot(s) that caught it together with the dmesg timestamp.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
D=/sys/kernel/debug/p7580/dump
try=0
while [ "$try" -lt 12 ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	SMOKE_DRAWS=2 SMOKE_W=64 SMOKE_H=64 /data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke \
		surfaceless >/dev/null 2>&1 &
	pid=$!
	hit=0
	while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
		s=$(cat "$D" 2>/dev/null)
		if printf '%s\n' "$s" | grep -qE 'status=0x0*8'; then
			printf 'attempt%s SNAPSHOT %s\n' "$try" \
				"$(printf '%s\n' "$s" | grep -E 'job_int|slot[0-2] status|last slot' | tr '\n' '|')"
			hit=1
		fi
	done
	wait "$pid"
	to=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' | grep -E 'TIMEOUT slot|recover-done|MMU fault' | sed 's/^\[[ 0-9.]*\] //' | cut -c1-130)
	if [ -n "$to" ]; then
		printf 'attempt%s dmesg: %s\n' "$try" "$(printf '%s' "$to" | tr '\n' ';')"
	fi
	[ "$hit" = 1 ] && break
	try=$((try + 1))
done
echo "tries=$try"

Your proof stands, and it can be made tighter: HEAD alone does not prove the header fetch succeeded (the JM latches HEAD_NEXT into HEAD at START, before it reads anything). With HEAD latched it means "dispatched, never reached execution", i.e. the fetch never completed. It is not "never started" and not a fault code.

To name the culprit, the instrument we still need is the shadow's refcount with a node index, because the winner is whichever put hits zero:
  in p7580_drv_shadow_put: pr_err("shadow_put iova=0x%llx refs=%d last=%d\n", sh->iova, atomic_read(&sh->refs), last) — print *before* the dec, plus the caller's node index if you can pass it (submit.c:1506-1520 is where the dec and the p7580_gem_gpu_unmap live).

content:
<irc>
Incoming IRC message from agent `KbaseCompare`:

Your reading is right about the *symptom chain*, but the log order you captured proves something stronger and reverses the causality: the chain's node 2 was not killed by its own fetch — it was *unmapped because the driver had already retired it*, and your own dispatch order is the proof.

The clincher is ordering. The fragment job (slot 0, seq=3) was dispatched *while node 2 (slot 1, seq=2) was still pending* — you see seq 0,1,2 then seq=3, and every post-start says ACTIVE/rawstat=0, i.e. nothing had completed yet. The fragment submit's node 0 depends on df->serial_prev, which is the chain's *last node's* fence (submit.c:2048, 2148). So for the fragment to be dispatched at all, node 2's fence must already have been signalled — with node 2 never having run. That is the bug, and everything else follows: shadow refs are atomic_set(&sh->refs, nodes) (submit.c:1479), so once the three nodes are "retired" the last put unmaps the page (p7580_drv_shadow_put -> p7580_gem_gpu_unmap, submit.c:1506-1520), and the JM's still-queued node-2 fetch then faults at +0x40 for the rest of the run. Recovery resets and draw 2 is clean — exactly what you see.

Why node 2's fence signalled early: the slot can hold more than one job, and the driver has exactly one bookkeeping slot for it.
 - panfrost7580_job.h:217 in_flight[P7580_NUM_JOB_SLOTS] is a single pointer per slot; hw_submit overwrites it (job.c:722) on every dispatch. Three back-to-back STARTs (your seq 0,1,2) leave in_flight[1] = node 2.
 - The dispatch gate only checks COMMAND_NEXT (WARN_ON, job.c:677), which is 0 once the JM has consumed a START into the current registers — so queueing a second and third job is allowed and unaccounted. kbase gates on kbasep_jm_is_js_free() AND kbdev->jm_slots[js].submitted_nr < BASE_JM_SUBMIT_SLOTS - 2 (mali_kbase_jm.h:47-71), and keeps a real per-slot submit queue.
 - The IRQ DONE leg retires exactly one job — the one in in_flight — and clears both bits (job.c:857-930). kbase derives how many jobs finished from JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE (0x1010) and retires that many, oldest first (mali_kbase_jm.c:377-405), then re-reads RAWSTAT (:408).

So the first DONE on slot 1 retired node 2, relaxed the fragment dependency, and dropped a shadow ref it should not have dropped. Corroboration from your previous two-slot dump: slot 1 read status 0x00 with no job in flight while its fetch was still retrying — the driver had already let go of it.

One 3-line experiment proves it on silicon, no rewrite: in the DONE leg print the retired job's seqno and JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE(0x1010). If you see "retire seq=2" as the first slot-1 completion (or seqno order 2,1,0 or 2 then nothing), the mis-retirement is confirmed on hardware. Combined with the shadow_put refcount print you already have queued, that closes both halves.

Fix order (parity with kbase, and each step is independently useful):
 1. Per-slot submit queue: oldest-first retirement, count from JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE, re-read RAWSTAT and loop.
 2. Gate dispatch the kbase way (submitted_nr cap), not on COMMAND_NEXT alone.
 3. Only then let the shadow go: the per-node refs are correct *if* retire order equals hardware order; until (1) lands, keep the shadow mapped for the slot's lifetime (one page per chain, per-file pool) so a bookkeeping slip can never unmap a page the GPU is reading.

On your trace_arm finding: confirmed and it matches the code — trace_arm resets jd->trace_left (the per-job dispatch/post-start lines printed, so that worked), while "chain jc=" is behind a separate static counter (p7580_chain_trace = 8, submit.c:155) that only a fresh boot restores. The dispatch jc values you now have are just as good: page-aligned base + 0x100 stride, 00010005/0002000b/0003000f = isolate's index rewrite, i.e. the shadow layout, and node2+0x40 again.
If response expected, reply via `write` (`path: "agent://KbaseCompare"`, `content: "…"`), when available; otherwise what you `yield` or say last this turn is delivered to `KbaseCompare` when you stop.
</irc>

If they continue with both slots idle, the tiler holds a stale descriptor pointer at fabric level.

Given (2), "wait for the last node's fence" is not a sufficient lifetime rule, because the consumer of a tiler descriptor is not the tiler job that was retired. Keep shadow pages mapped for the file's lifetime (one page per chain, per-file pool, round-robin by submit counter) and unmap only at file close after the slots are quiescent. That is also what kbase does — regions are released only when no job that can touch them remains, not when the producing job's fence fires.

Incoming IRC message from agent `KbaseCompare`:

That burst kills the phase theory cleanly (09/29 interleaved within 64 ms, all after the fragment dispatch, none before), and it closes the case as far as the driver is concerned. Consolidated verdict and the fix list, since this is the whole picture:

MECHANISM. A TILER descriptor page is unmapped when the tiler job's own fence signals, but the descriptor is still consumed downstream: the fragment job's tile iteration runs on the tiler block and re-reads the tiler job's Draw state (offset 0x40 — your arithmetic, and the only field a consumer outside the tiler job needs). When that internal copy is still resident the fragment sails through (draw 2: fence 82 ms after dispatch, zero faults); when it is not, the block re-reads a page that was freed 191 ms earlier, retries 9 times in 64 ms, and the fragment job never retires (ACTIVE 0x08, stat/rawstat 0 → the 750 ms timeout). Coin flip per draw, exactly as observed. That this is a lifetime rule and not a mapping bug is now proven on all sides: leaf correct, chain phase clean, retirement in order, reader appears with the fragment.

This is also the same class as the KWin stall (0xb2aa000, translation READ during a fragment job, ACTIVE 0x08, stat 0). One bug family, two workloads.

FIX LIST, in dependency order (all kbase-parity, none speculative):
1. panfrost7580_job.c:847 — move the JSn_STATUS/HEAD/TAIL reads ABOVE the JOB_INT_CLEAR write (job.c:852 currently reads after). kbase reads STATUS then clears (mali_kbase_jm.c:337-346). Until this lands nobody can trust any js_status in a capture; after it, a real DONE reads 0x01.
2. Shadow lifetime (the actual bug): stop unmapping shadow descriptor pages at the producer's fence. p7580_drv_shadow_put (submit.c:1506-1520) must not call p7580_gem_gpu_unmap; keep a per-file shadow pool (one page per chain, round-robin by submit counter) and unmap only at file close after the slots are quiescent. #!/bin/sh
# Knob matrix on the shipped Mesa 20.3.5 stack:
#  A: DRAWS=2 with SMOKE_GAP_MS 0/100/500  (lifetime vs decaying-copy test)
#  B: DRAWS=1 repeated                 (per-draw hang probability)
#  C: DRAWS=2 with SMOKE_PAD=1024      (is the rate allocator-layout dependent?)
# Prints one compact line per run: faults, timeouts, whether the fragment fence
# signalled, and any OVERLAP / tiler-idle warnings.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke

run() { # label draws gap pad
	lbl=$1; draws=$2; gap=$3; pad=$4
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_DRAWS=$draws SMOKE_GAP_MS=$gap SMOKE_PAD=$pad \
		SMOKE_W=64 SMOKE_H=64 timeout 30 "$S" surfaceless >/dev/null 2>&1
	d=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg')
	f=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -c 'MMU fault')
	t=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot')
	ff=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -c 'fence signal slot=0')
	ov=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -c 'OVERLAP')
	ti=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -ci 'did not idle')
	printf '%-18s faults=%-3s timeouts=%s frag_fence=%s overlap=%s tiler_idle=%s\n' \
		"$lbl" "$f" "$t" "$ff" "$ov" "$ti"
}

i=0
while [ $i -lt 5 ]; do run "A gap=0 #$i"   2 0    0;    i=$((i+1)); done
i=0
while [ $i -lt 5 ]; do run "A gap=100 #$i" 2 100  0;    i=$((i+1)); done
i=0
while [ $i -lt 5 ]; do run "A gap=500 #$i" 2 500  0;    i=$((i+1)); done
i=0
while [ $i -lt 8 ]; do run "B draws=1 #$i" 1 0    0;    i=$((i+1)); done
i=0
while [ $i -lt 4 ]; do run "C pad=1024 #$i" 2 0   1024; i=$((i+1)); done

Incoming IRC message from agent `KbaseCompare`:

The matrix refines the model rather than breaking it, and your gap result is the most valuable thing in it. One inconsistency to fix and three conclusions.

First, a counting bug on your side: gap=100 shows frag_fence=1 in 5/5 runs but timeouts=1/5. Eight missing fence signals cannot coexist with one slot timeout. Either the probe exits before the second draw's fragment fence (then the count means "seen within the run window") or the fence lines are being deduplicated. Make those two columns consistent or state per-draw "fence observed within window", otherwise the rate columns cannot be compared across cells.

Three conclusions.

1. Freeing the page is necessary but not sufficient. Your three cells now show three independent conditions, and each is a knob you already have:
   - the descriptor page must be freed (the lifetime rule) — fix (2);
   - the consumer must still need the content: the internal copy decays, hence stall rate 1/5 at gap 0-100 vs 5/5 at 500 with faults constant (the hardware prefetches the Draw block, the dropped read is harmless while the internal copy is valid, fatal once it has decayed);

#!/bin/sh
# Resolve the gap=100 fence/timeout counting: keep probe stdout and list every
# dispatch/fence/timeout line in order for each run.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 3 ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_DRAWS=2 SMOKE_GAP_MS=100 SMOKE_W=64 SMOKE_H=64 timeout 30 "$S" \
		surfaceless > /data/mesa203-build/mx-out-$i.txt 2>&1
	echo "rc=$?"
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > /data/mesa203-build/mx-dm-$i.txt
	echo "--- run $i: probe says ---"
	grep -E 'dispatch [0-9]+/|RESULT|SMOKE: \[' /data/mesa203-build/mx-out-$i.txt | tail -5
	echo "--- run $i: kernel order ---"
	grep -E 'dispatch slot=|fence signal|TIMEOUT slot|MMU fault' \
		/data/mesa203-build/mx-dm-$i.txt |
		sed 's/^\[ *\([0-9.]*\)\]/\1/;s/ p7580_job: / /;s/ MMU fault AS0: / MMU-FAULT /' |
		cut -c1-110
	i=$((i + 1))
done

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Contended matrix on kernel #43 (kwin_wayland holds renderD128 on system Mesa 26).
# Existence-only attribution: our submits are the dispatch lines with seq<=40
# (our file starts at seq 0); TIMEOUT/fence lines are matched against that jc
# set, fault lines against the page of each of our jcs. No rates are claimed.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
T=/tmp/mx
mkdir -p "$T"
KB=$(uname -a | cut -d' ' -f1-9)
FD=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'ls -l /proc/*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c renderD128')
echo "### $KB  renderD128_fds=$FD  contended-with: $(pgrep -x kwin_wayland | tr '\n' ' ')"

run() { # label draws gap pad [W H]
	lbl=$1; draws=$2; gap=$3; pad=$4
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_DRAWS=$draws SMOKE_GAP_MS=$gap SMOKE_PAD=$pad \
		SMOKE_W=${5:-64} SMOKE_H=${6:-64} timeout 40 "$S" surfaceless \
		>"$T/out" 2>&1
	rc=$?
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$T/dm"
	# our jc set: dispatch lines with seq<=40
	grep 'dispatch slot=' "$T/dm" |
		sed -n 's/.*seq=\([0-9]\+\) .*jc=0x\([0-9a-f]*\).*/\1 \2/p' |
		awk '$1<=40 {print "0x"$2}' | sort -u > "$T/ourjc"
	njc=$(wc -l < "$T/ourjc")
	# our pages (jc with low 3 hex digits zeroed)
	sed 's/...$//' "$T/ourjc" > "$T/ourpg"
	# own timeouts: TIMEOUT line jc in our set
	ot=0
	while read -r j; do
		[ -n "$j" ] && grep -q "jc=$j" "$T/dm" && grep 'TIMEOUT slot' "$T/dm" |
			grep -q "jc=$j" && ot=$((ot+1))
	done < "$T/ourjc"
	tt=$(grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot' "$T/dm")
	# own faults: fault addr page in our page set
	of=0
	for a in $(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat [0-9a-f]* addr 0*\([0-9a-f]\{3\}\)\([0-9a-f]*\).*/\2/p' "$T/dm" | sed 's/^/0x/'); do
		grep -qx "$a" "$T/ourpg" && of=$((of+1))
	done
	tf=$(grep -c 'MMU fault' "$T/dm")
	ff=$(grep -c 'fence signal slot=0' "$T/dm")
	printf '%-22s rc=%s own_jc=%-2s own_timeout=%s own_fault=%s | all: timeout=%s fault=%s | frag_fence_all=%s\n' \
		"$lbl" "$rc" "$njc" "$ot" "$of" "$tt" "$tf" "$ff"
}

i=0; while [ $i -lt 20 ]; do run "D1 #$i" 1 0 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 10 ]; do run "D2 #$i" 2 0 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 5 ];  do run "D2 gap500 #$i" 2 500 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 5 ];  do run "D2 gap500 pad #$i" 2 500 1024; i=$((i+1)); done
run "720x1280" 1 0 0 720 1280

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Contended existence-only matrix, kernel #43. Our submits are the dispatch
# lines with seq<=40 (our DRM file's seq counter starts at 0); KWin's are the
# high-seq lines from its own file. Faults are attributed by the page of our jc.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
T=/tmp/mx
mkdir -p "$T"
KB=$(uname -a | cut -d' ' -f1-9)
FD=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'ls -l /proc/*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c renderD128')
KW=$(pgrep -x kwin_wayland | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "### $KB | renderD128_fds=$FD | kwin=$KW"
echo "### job.c sha256 6c499118f0e9761ee753a3f9a183b28ed0e5f6ebba990f1b7a637e8a48728c41 (75757B 22:12) | submit.c 505be084..f81a3b5 (80467B Nov25)"

run() { # label draws gap pad [W H]
	lbl=$1; draws=$2; gap=$3; pad=$4
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_DRAWS=$draws SMOKE_GAP_MS=$gap SMOKE_PAD=$pad \
		SMOKE_W=${5:-64} SMOKE_H=${6:-64} timeout 40 "$S" surfaceless \
		>"$T/out" 2>&1
	rc=$?
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$T/dm"

	grep 'dispatch slot=' "$T/dm" |
		sed -n 's/.*jc=0x\([0-9a-f]*\) .*seq=\([0-9]\+\).*/\2 \1/p' |
		awk '$1<=40 {print "0x"$2}' | sort -u > "$T/ourjc"
	awk '{print $1}' <(sed -n 's/.*fence signal slot=[0-9] seq=\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p' "$T/dm") >/dev/null 2>&1

	# own fences: fence lines whose seq is one of ours (seq<=40 in a dispatch)
	sed -n 's/.*jc=0x[0-9a-f]* .*seq=\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p' "$T/dm" | awk '$1<=40' | sort -u > "$T/ourseq"
	of_fence=0
	while read -r q; do
		[ -n "$q" ] && grep -q "fence signal slot=0 seq=$q " "$T/dm" && of_fence=$((of_fence+1))
	done < "$T/ourseq"

	# own timeouts: TIMEOUT line whose jc is ours
	ot=0
	while read -r j; do
		[ -n "$j" ] && grep 'TIMEOUT slot' "$T/dm" | grep -q "jc=$j" && ot=$((ot+1))
	done < "$T/ourjc"
	tt=$(grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot' "$T/dm")

	# own faults: fault addr page equals the page of one of our jcs
	sed 's/...$//' "$T/ourjc" > "$T/ourpg"
	of=0
	for a in $(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat [0-9a-f]* addr 0*\([0-9a-f]\{4\}\)$/\1/p' "$T/dm" | sed 's/^/0x/'); do
		grep -qx "$a" "$T/ourpg" && of=$((of+1))
	done
	tf=$(grep -c 'MMU fault' "$T/dm")
	lat=$(grep -o 'recover-done.*latched=0x[0-9a-f]*' "$T/dm" | sed 's/.*latched=//' | tr '\n' ',' )

	printf '%-20s rc=%s own_jc=%-2s own_fence=%s own_timeout=%s own_fault=%s | foreign: timeout=%s fault=%s | latched=%s\n' \
		"$lbl" "$rc" "$(wc -l < "$T/ourjc")" "$of_fence" "$ot" "$of" \
		"$((tt-ot))" "$((tf-of))" "${lat:-none}"
}

i=0; while [ $i -lt 15 ]; do run "D1 #$i" 1 0 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 8 ];  do run "D2 #$i" 2 0 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 5 ];  do run "D2 gap500 #$i" 2 500 0; i=$((i+1)); done
i=0; while [ $i -lt 5 ];  do run "D2 g500pad #$i" 2 500 1024; i=$((i+1)); done
run "720x1280" 1 0 0 720 1280

Verified the mmu.c change that #43 carries, and then a correction to my own framing that your numbers force.

Your first instinct was right.

Now the correction. All 34 runs are fault-free in our own pages, yet D2 still stalls 7/8 with latched=0x00. So on #43 the probe's stall is NOT the translation stall — the fault cannot be its cause if it is absent while the stall remains. The honest reading is that the node2+0x40 translation fault I traced in dm-arm-1 was a *dependent walk* of the AF-fault retry path: AF made the block re-walk, the re-walk hit the (genuinely) freed shadow page, and that is what I measured. Remove AF, the extra walks vanish, and so does the observable fault — while the real stall persists. Consequences: (a) the shadow page is still being unmapped while a consumer may read it — the latent bug stands, and fix 4 is still correct; (b) it must NOT be validated by this probe's stall count, only by KWin's fault stream, which you measure at 1-43 faults per window; (c) my "one mechanism" statement was wrong and the lifetime finding is a latent-defect finding, not the stall explanation.

What the probe now measures is a different defect, and its signature is exact: timeout with latched=0x00 (slot idle, job not active), no fault, missing fence, 750 ms latency. That is the port's own documented dispatch-bail case: p7580_job_hw_submit bails on WARN_ON(JS_COMMAND_NEXT) (job.c:677) leaving the job unqueued and its fence unsignalled until the timeout handler signals it — the comment at job.c:1130-1142 describes precisely this ("hw_submit WARN_ON bail leaves the new fence unsignaled"). Checks, all from existing output: grep for "WARNING" in each run; count "dispatch slot=" lines per run against the jobs you submitted (a bailed job prints nothing); and see whether the missing job is always one dispatched while the previous job still held the next register. If so, the fix is to not bail — wait bounded for COMMAND_NEXT to drain or return an error drm_sched retries — and signal the fence immediately when a job is not queued.

Two measurement notes: your 12/15 D1 runs with neither fence nor timeout is a window artefact (the probe exits before the log flushes) — wait for the fence or hold the capture open. And Main's "wallpaper on glass, 0 faults" is consistent with your own 6 s idle negative: the KWin class needs active rendering, so the lifetime-fix validation must capture KWin mid-animation, not idle.

#!/bin/sh
# Does the #43 stall involve a dispatch bail? A bailed hw_submit prints no
# "dispatch slot=" line, so compare dispatched jc count against the 9 jobs a
# DRAWS=2 run submits (3+4 chain nodes + 2 fragments), and look for WARNINGs.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
D=/data/mesa203-build
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 4 ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_DRAWS=2 SMOKE_W=64 SMOKE_H=64 timeout 40 "$S" surfaceless >"$D/bail-out-$i.txt" 2>&1
	rc=$?
	sleep 0.3
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$D/bail-dm-$i.txt"
	w=$(grep -c 'WARNING' "$D/bail-dm-$i.txt")
	nd=$(grep -c 'dispatch slot=' "$D/bail-dm-$i.txt")
	nf=$(grep -c 'fence signal' "$D/bail-dm-$i.txt")
	nt=$(grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot' "$D/bail-dm-$i.txt")
	printf 'run%s rc=%s dispatches=%s fences=%s timeouts=%s warnings=%s | probe:%s\n' \
		"$i" "$rc" "$nd" "$nf" "$nt" "$w" \
		"$(grep -c 'dispatch [0-9]/2 done' "$D/bail-out-$i.txt") draws-done"
	i=$((i + 1))
done
echo "--- ordered events of run0 ---"
grep -E 'dispatch slot=|fence signal|TIMEOUT slot|WARNING|MMU fault' "$D/bail-dm-0.txt" |
	sed 's/^\[ *\([0-9.]*\)\]/\1/;s/ p7580_job: / /;s/ panfrost.*panfrost7580: / /' |
	cut -c1-96 | head -30

content.thinking:
Peer asks for three forward-looking improvements:
1. Add VOID class to measurement protocol.
2. Fix probe: assert per-draw fence (drmSyncobjWait / WAIT_BO) instead of relying on glFinish, exit non-zero if missing.
3. Print exact VA list per window (not "family").

Items 2 and 3 are concrete userspace improvements I can implement now, and 1 is a classification rule I can encode in the script. This is a good, bounded final piece of work: upgrade the probe to (a) take the render target BO fd and wait on it with DRM_IOCTL_PANFROST_WAIT_BO (or drmSyncobjWait on the out fence? Mesa's panfrost doesn't expose the out fence to userspace...).

Hmm: how can a userspace client verify the GPU completed a draw? Options:
- gbm_bo / GL: after glFinish(), no userspace-visible fence. Mesa's glFinish calls panfrost_batch_submit and waits on the fence internally — if the fence is signalled by the recovery, glFinish returns "successfully" (that's the masking).
- A stronger check: render to a GBM BO, then use the BO's dma-buf implicit fence (DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC? or drmPrimeHandleToFD + sync_file?). Mesa's gbm bo has no sync_file export.
- Alternative: use `glFenceSync` + `glClientWaitSync` — GLES2 doesn't have fences; GLES3 does. Our context is ES2 (EGL_CONTEXT_CLIENT_VERSION 2). Could request ES3? Renderer supports ES 3.0. glFenceSync in ES3 requires the extension/version: Mesa 20.3.5 with ES3 context supports glFenceSync. But that fence is Mesa's own and would be signalled the same way (via the recovered fence), so it wouldn't detect the loss.
- Real detection: check that the *result* is correct. E.g. render a known pattern and verify the pixels (deterministic checksum). Earlier checksums alternated, indicating garbage. A robust probe could render a solid color and assert all sampled pixels equal the expected value; a dropped/stalled job would read stale/garbage → mismatch → non-zero exit. That's a concrete, achievable check and it's *content-based*, immune to fence masking.

So: implement "verify" mode: clear to black, draw a full-screen triangle with constant color (e.g. (0.25,0.5,0.75,1)), glFinish, glReadPixels a 16x16 block at center, and assert every pixel equals the expected quantized value (RGBA4 → 0x4400/0x8800/0xCC00? With RGBA4, 0.25→4/15→0x44..., 0.5→8/15→0x88, 0.75→12/15? 0.75*15=11.25→11=0xB). Better use RGBA8 renderbuffer (GL_RGBA8 via GL_OES_rgb8_rgba8? ES2 has GL_RGBA4/565; ES3 has RGBA8). Simpler: keep RGBA4 and compare against the value observed in the *first* successful run? Not robust.

Alternative: draw with a shader that writes a constant, then assert all 256 pixels in the read window are identical to each other (not to a specific value). A stalled/partial job would leave either zeros (cleared black) or mixed data → not all-equal-to-expected-color. Since we clear to black and draw the constant color, a correct render has all pixels = C (nonzero, since C = 0.5,0.5,0.5 → RGBA4 0x8). Garbage would be random/stale. Assert: all pixels equal each other AND equal (supported) a specific value derived from the first pixel. That detects "didn't render" (all zeros = clear only) vs rendered.

That's implementable: modify render_once to use a constant-color shader when SMOKE_VERIFY=1, read 16x16, and check all bytes equal to the first pixel's bytes and nonzero.

Plus report exit code non-zero if verification fails.

3. Print exact VA list: my scripts already print addresses in some captures; I can add to the matrix script a per-run "foreign VA list" (sorted unique) and our VA list.

1. VOID classification: compute per run: foreign_recover = count of recover-done lines whose ... hmm recover-done has no jc; but I can infer: a recover-done line exists while no own timeout line exists → likely foreign recovery → VOID. Rule: PASS = own fence for every dispatched job AND own_fault=0 AND no recover-done beyond our own timeouts; VOID = recover-done count > own_timeout count; FAIL = own_fault>0 or own_timeout>0.

Let me implement:
- Probe: add SMOKE_VERIFY=1 → constant-color shader + uniformity check + nonzero exit on failure; also print the observed pixel value.
- Script: three-valued verdict + exact VA lists (own/foreign).

Then run a small set (say 6 D2 runs) to demonstrate the machinery and report. That's a solid final deliverable: improved probe + verdict classifier.

Time: probe change ~15 min of careful edits; risk of breaking the working probe. Keep changes additive and default-off (SMOKE_VERIFY only). Let me implement carefully.

render_once currently builds vs/fs from globals. For verify, use a different pair:
vs: same triangle.
fs: "precision mediump float; void main(){ gl_FragColor = vec4(0.5,0.25,0.75,1.0); }"
Then read 16x16 RGBA bytes; expected RGBA4 quantization: 0.5→8 (0x88), 0.25→4 (0x44), 0.75→11 (0xBB), 1.0→15 (0xFF). With dithering, values may vary ±1. So assert: all pixels equal each other within ±0x11 tolerance and nonzero alpha. Simpler: compute min/max per channel across the 256 pixels; require max-min <= 0x11 and center pixel nonzero.

Report: print "verify: uniform=1 minmax=..." and set a flag for exit code.

Implement:
- In render_once, if SMOKE_VERIFY: use verify shaders, then after readpixels compute uniformity, print, and return h (nonzero) but also set global verify_fail flag.
- main: rc |= verify_fail.

Let me code it.

Given the effort, and that the deliverable is complete, this is optional polish — but the peer explicitly asked to fix the probe so "returned 0" doesn't mask the defect. Doing it is valuable and bounded.

Let me implement now.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# KWin mid-animation capture (read-only; run only when Main says the animation
# is up). Records dmesg + per-second debugfs slot dumps + an attribution header.
#   rootshell /bin/sh /data/mesa203-build/kwin-cap.sh [seconds]
secs=${1:-20}
O=/data/mesa203-build
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
hdr="$O/kwin-cap-$stamp.header"
log="$O/kwin-cap-$stamp.txt"
{
	echo "captured: $(date)"
	uname -a
	echo "renderD128 fds: $(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'ls -l /proc/*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c renderD128')"
	echo "kwin pid: $(pgrep -x kwin_wayland | tr '\n' ' ')"
	echo "kwin mesa env lines: $(rootshell /bin/sh -c "tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -x kwin_wayland)/environ 2>/dev/null" | grep -cE 'LD_LIBRARY_PATH|MESA203')"
	echo "job.c sha256: $(sha256sum /lib/modules/*/panfrost7580* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
	echo "job_timeout_ms: $(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'cat /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/job_timeout_ms 2>/dev/null')"
	echo "proc: $(pgrep -a kwin_wayland | head -1)"
} > "$hdr" 2>&1
rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt "$secs" ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'cat /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/dump' >/dev/null 2>&1
	sleep 1
	i=$((i + 1))
done
rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$log"
va=$(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat \([0-9a-f]*\) addr 0*\([0-9a-f]*\)/\2 \1/p' "$log" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10)
{
	cat "$hdr"
	echo "--- counts ---"
	echo "MMU faults: $(grep -c 'MMU fault' "$log")"
	echo "TRANSLATION: $(grep -c 'TRANSLATION_FAULT' "$log")  ACCESS_FLAG: $(grep -c 'ACCESS_FLAG' "$log")"
	echo "TIMEOUT: $(grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot' "$log")  recover-done: $(grep -c 'recover-done' "$log")"
	echo "OVERLAP: $(grep -c 'OVERLAP' "$log")  tiler-idle: $(grep -ci 'did not idle' "$log")"
	echo "--- top VAs (count stat) ---"
	echo "$va"
	echo "--- distinct VAs ---"
	sed -n 's/.*addr 0*\([0-9a-f]*\)$/\1/p' "$log" | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '
	echo
} | tee "$O/kwin-cap-$stamp.summary"
echo "files: $hdr $log $O/kwin-cap-$stamp.summary"

Your fragment dispatch→fence latency metric will see it; if you run 720x1280 with Mesa 26, record the very first dispatch separately from the steady-state ones.

That also makes fix 4's shape obvious and consistent: the invariant should be "a live BO always has leaves; leaves are dropped only when the object's last user is gone" — map_file_bos puts the shadow outside the file idr, so the shadow still needs its own pool (map once, never unmap before file close). Same rule, two mechanisms.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# N=30 at 720x1280, content-verified, on the post-map_file_bos build.
# Under map_file_bos a fault count is NOT evidence of correctness (the mapping
# gives leaves to BOs the GPU would otherwise fault on), so the verdict is:
#   PASS = content verify OK + own fence for the draw + no own timeout + no
#          foreign recover-done inside the run window
#   VOID = foreign recover-done / animation restart inside the window
#   FAIL = verify MISMATCH or own TIMEOUT or probe rc != 0
# First fragment dispatch is reported separately from steady state: the first
# dispatch pays the whole-file mapping (incl. the 128 MB tiler heap).
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
D=/data/mesa203-build
N=${1:-30}
echo "### $(uname -a | cut -d' ' -f1-9) | fds=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'ls -l /proc/*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c renderD128') | kwin=$(pgrep -x kwin_wayland | tr '\n' ' ')"
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt "$N" ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	SMOKE_VERIFY=1 SMOKE_DRAWS=1 timeout 60 "$S" surfaceless >"$D/v720-$i.out" 2>&1
	rc=$?
	sleep 0.2
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$D/v720-$i.dm"
	verdict=$(grep -o 'verify uniform=[0-9] nonzero=[0-9].*' "$D/v720-$i.out" | tail -1)
	case "$verdict" in *OK) v=PASS ;; *MISMATCH) v=FAIL ;; *) v=FAIL ;; esac
	grep -q 'TIMEOUT slot' "$D/v720-$i.dm" && v=FAIL
	grep -q 'recover-done' "$D/v720-$i.dm" && [ "$v" = PASS ] && v=VOID
	[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && v=FAIL
	lat=$(awk '
		/dispatch slot=0/ { if (!d) { d=$1; seqd=$0 } }
		/fence signal slot=0/ { if (d && !f) { f=1; print $1-d } }
	' "$D/v720-$i.dm" | head -1)
	printf 'run%-2s %-4s rc=%s first_disp_to_fence=%ss %s\n' "$i" "$v" "$rc" "${lat:-n/a}" \
		"$(printf '%s' "$verdict" | sed 's/verify //')"
	i=$((i + 1))
done

Very interesting results, but the classification logic has a bug: many runs show FAIL with content verify OK. Why? My script:
```
case "$verdict" in *OK) v=PASS ;; *MISMATCH) v=FAIL ;; *) v=FAIL ;; esac
grep -q 'TIMEOUT slot' && v=FAIL
grep -q 'recover-done' && [ "$v" = PASS ] && v=VOID
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && v=FAIL
```
FAIL with rc=0 and OK verify means: `grep -q 'TIMEOUT slot'` matched → v=FAIL. So those runs had TIMEOUT lines (KWin's or ours?) — I didn't attribute in this script! I set v=FAIL on ANY TIMEOUT line regardless of owner. And recover-done → VOID only if PASS.

- 28/30: content OK.
- first_disp_to_fence=n/a everywhere: my awk failed (probably because dmesg had no dispatch lines for our jobs — trace budget exhausted? We don't re-arm trace_arm in this script! I removed it? - Also KWin window: 0 faults, 0 timeouts during the 20 s capture.

#!/bin/sh
# N=30 at 720x1280 on the #44 map_file_bos image, content-verified, attributed.
# Our jc set = dispatch lines with seq<=10 (our DRM file's seq starts at 0);
# KWin's submits carry high seq numbers. Faults attributed by the page of our jc.
# Verdict: FAIL = verify MISMATCH | own_timeout | own_fault | rc!=0
#          VOID = foreign recover-done inside the run window
#          PASS = none of the above
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
D=/data/mesa203-build
N=${1:-30}
echo "### $(uname -v) | fds=$(rootshell /bin/sh -c 'ls -l /proc/*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c renderD128') | kwin=$(pgrep -x kwin_wayland | tr '\n' ' ')"
pass=0; fail=0; void=0
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt "$N" ]; do
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg -c >/dev/null'
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/trace_arm' >/dev/null 2>&1
	SMOKE_VERIFY=1 SMOKE_DRAWS=1 timeout 60 "$S" surfaceless >"$D/w-$i.out" 2>&1
	rc=$?
	sleep 0.2
	rootshell /bin/sh -c 'dmesg' > "$D/w-$i.dm"
	grep 'dispatch slot=' "$D/w-$i.dm" |
		sed -n 's/.*jc=0x\([0-9a-f]*\) .*seq=\([0-9]\+\).*/\2 \1/p' |
		awk '$1<=10 {print "0x"$2}' | sort -u > "$D/w-$i.jc"
	sed 's/...$//' "$D/w-$i.jc" > "$D/w-$i.pg"
	ot=0
	while read -r j; do [ -n "$j" ] && grep 'TIMEOUT slot' "$D/w-$i.dm" | grep -q "jc=$j" && ot=$((ot+1)); done < "$D/w-$i.jc"
	of=0
	while read -r a; do [ -n "$a" ] && grep -qx "$a" "$D/w-$i.pg" && of=$((of+1)); done <<-EOF
	$(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat [0-9a-f]* addr 0*\([0-9a-f]\{4\}\)$/\1/p' "$D/w-$i.dm" | sed 's/^/0x/')
	EOF
	tt=$(grep -c 'TIMEOUT slot' "$D/w-$i.dm")
	rec=$(grep -c 'recover-done' "$D/w-$i.dm")
	ver=$(grep -o 'verify .*' "$D/w-$i.out" | tail -1)
	v=PASS
	case "$ver" in *MISMATCH*) v=FAIL ;; esac
	[ "$ot" -gt 0 ] && v=FAIL
	[ "$of" -gt 0 ] && v=FAIL
	[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && v=FAIL
	[ "$v" = PASS ] && [ "$rec" -gt 0 ] && v=VOID
	case "$v" in PASS) pass=$((pass+1));; FAIL) fail=$((fail+1));; void) :;; *) void=$((void+1));; esac
	[ "$v" = VOID ] && void=$((void+1))
	lat=$(awk '/dispatch slot=0/{if(!d)d=$1}/fence signal slot=0/{if(d&&!f){f=1;printf "%.3f",$1-d}}' "$D/w-$i.dm")
	printf 'run%-2s %-4s rc=%s own_fault=%s own_timeout=%s foreign_timeout=%s rec=%s disp2fence=%s %s\n' \
		"$i" "$v" "$rc" "$of" "$ot" "$((tt-ot))" "$rec" "${lat:-n/a}" \
		"$(printf '%s' "$ver" | sed 's/verify //')"
	i=$((i + 1))
done
echo "TOTAL pass=$pass fail=$fail void=$void"

of=0

$(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat [0-9a-f]* addr 0*\([0-9a-f]\{4\}\)$/\1/p' "$D/w-$i.dm" | sed 's/^/0x/')

Bug: takes last 4 hex digits. Fix: extract the *high* part of the address (all but last 3 hex digits), i.e. page = addr >> 12. Implement: sed get full addr, then shell arithmetic: `printf '0x%x' $((0x$addr & ~0xfff))`? In busybox ash, arithmetic with 64-bit hex works.

Better approach: extract full address (strip leading zeros), then compute page with awk:
```
awk -v a="$addr" 'BEGIN{printf "0x%x", strtonum(a) - (strtonum(a)%4096)}'  # strtonum is gawk-only
```
busybox awk lacks strtonum. Alternative: sed-based page extraction: address hex string, drop last 3 hex chars, prepend 0x. That works if address has >3 digits (always).

```
for a in $(sed -n 's/.*MMU fault AS0: [A-Z_]*\/[A-Z]* stat [0-9a-f]* addr 0*\([0-9a-f]*\)$/\1/p' "$D/w-$i.dm"); do
    pg="0x$(echo "$a" | sed 's/...$//')"    # drops last 3 hex digits → page (4 KiB)
    grep -qx "$pg" "$D/w-$i.pg" && of=$((of+1))
done
```
Careful: `sed 's/...$//'` drops last 3 chars — yes hex digits. And our .pg file was built with `sed 's/...$//'` on the jc (same operation) — consistent.

#!/bin/sh
# N x 720x1280 on the current image, content-verified and attributed.
# Classifier is self-tested against recorded positives before any run.
#
# Attribution: our jc set = dispatch lines with seq<=10 (our DRM file's seq
# starts at 0; other clients carry high seq). A fault is OURS when the 4 KiB
# page of its VA (va & ~0xFFF) is the page of one of our jc.
# Verdict: FAIL = verify MISMATCH | own_timeout | own_fault | rc!=0
#          VOID = foreign recover-done inside the run window
#          PASS = none of the above
#
# FALSIFICATION CONDITIONS (descriptor-lifetime mechanism):
#  - a fault at a VA never mapped-then-unmapped falsifies "freed page still read";
#  - shadow kept mapped + N content-verified runs still failing => lifetime
#    necessary but not sufficient (defect is consumer-side);
#  - map_file_bos clearing the fault stream while content verify fails =>
#    faults masked, not fixed.
. /data/mesa203-env.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
S=/data/mesa203-build/mesa203-smoke
D=/data/mesa203-build
N=${1:-30}

# --- classifier: page of VA vs a page list -------------------------------
classify() { # addr pagesfile -> own|foreign
	pg="0x$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/...$//')"
	grep -qx "$pg" "$2" && echo own || echo foreign
}

Classifier is right; one review note on the experiment's shape, because as described it will not test what we want and could produce a false negative.
